root_cause_criterion.missing_conjunct: `nread != 0` before `pkt[mq->npacket++] = byte` and `byte & 0x80` may consume the read result
root_cause_criterion.criterion: After `Curl_read(conn, sockfd, (char *)&byte, 1, &nread)` returns in `MQTT_REMAINING_LENGTH`, `mqtt_doing()` must require `nread != 0` before treating `byte` as a received remaining-length octet.
root_cause_criterion.description: The vulnerable original falls through this guard with `nread == 0`, so the one-byte local `byte` remains unwritten and later code still stores and branches on it. The fixed logic stops at the same site when no byte was written.
root_cause_criterion.verification_note: The vulnerable original trace records `remaining_length_guard.nread=0` and still executes the protected `remaining_length_store` event, so the required assertion is violated at the root site. The fixed original reaches the same root event with `nread=0` but omits the protected store and sink (`guarded`). The closest source-grounded perturbation `response0_connack` produces `nread=1` and executes `remaining_length_store` and `remaining_length_sink` on both sides, supplying the genuine witness.

nodes.state: At `pkt[mq->npacket++] = byte`, the one-byte local `byte` has only `nread` initialized bytes from the immediately preceding `Curl_read`, so when `nread < sizeof(byte)` the store copies a byte whose initialized prefix is too short for the full one-byte write.

At `while (byte & 0x80)`, the branch consumes one byte from the same local `byte`, but the initialized prefix recorded for that slot is still shorter than `sizeof(byte)`, matching MemorySanitizer's one-byte uninitialized read.

edges.relation: The same stack slot `byte` whose write the missing `nread != 0` guard should guarantee is the byte later copied into `pkt[mq->npacket++]` after the guard falls through.

The same local `byte` slot copied at `pkt[mq->npacket++] = byte` is immediately re-read by the `while (byte & 0x80)` sink condition, so the uninitialized-byte state persists directly into the sanitizer sink.
